changes: p2 Pūrṇānandanātha: removed 'nātha' from titles (it is part of the Kaula initiatory name, kept in the name); confidence lowered to low because the teacher role is inferred only from a homage formula
date.month: Māgha kept only as a tentative reading of corrupt 'mākhaṃṇḍe'; the uncertainty is now explained in notes
notes: added the metrical analysis and the possibility that a year chronogram is hidden in the corrupt pāda

notes: The date and scribe passage is an anuṣṭubh verse: '[mākhaṃṇḍe] māsi site pakṣe bhṛgu[ra]vāsarasaṃmite / jagaṃnāthena likhitaṃ pustakaṃ sādhakāptaye'. 'mākhaṃṇḍe' is corrupt. It may stand for Māgha, or it may be what is left of a year chronogram (bhūtasaṃkhyā). No year can be recovered, so the month is only tentative. 'bhṛguravāsara' should be read as bhṛguvāsara (Friday). Pūrṇānandanātha is named only in a homage ('namaḥ'). The -ānandanātha initiatory name in a Śrīvidyā text suggests he was the scribe's guru, but the colophon does not say so. He could also be a lineage figure, and possibly the well-known Tantric author Pūrṇānanda.
